disposition_reason: Table 3 prints wet-weight cadmium, arsenic, lead, mercury, nickel, chromium and aluminum in house crickets from seven diet groups; the text prints selected dry-matter values.

study.design: two controlled feeding trials (7 and 15 days) with seaweed-enriched diets, 3 rearing replicates per group
study.origin: commercial insect farm colonies, Montecassiano, Italy
study.method: lyophilization, microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion; GF-AAS (Agilent 240Z, Zeeman) for Cd, As, Pb, Ni, Cr, Al; direct mercury analyzer (DMA-1) for Hg; clean room
lod: LOD/LOQ measured but not printed in the main text

findings.notes: Mean ± SD (n = 9: 3 rearing replicates x 3 aliquots); crickets fasted 24 h before slaughter; experimental diets at a commercial insect farm in Italy; wet weight.

unresolved: Trial 1 cadmium: text says no significant differences on DM basis, but Table 3 (WW) marks PP10 (0.050) as significantly higher.
Other per-diet DM values are figure-only (Figs 1-2).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU limits cited: Reg. (EU) 2022/188 house cricket novel food spec Cd ≤0.05, Pb ≤0.06 mg/kg; meat Cd 0.05, Pb 0.1; rice As 0.2; fish Hg 0.5; seaweed Ni 30 mg/kg
